---
title: Local documentation
---

Read the documentation for the DASCore installed in your project's Python environment:

```bash
python -m dascore doc
python -m dascore doc Patch.select
python -m dascore doc Spool.chunk
python -m dascore doc Patch.viz.waterfall
python -m dascore doc recipes/tunnel_inventory
```

`dascore doc` is the equivalent console command. Without a target it reports the DASCore version, Python executable, package location, and documentation directory. For repeated agent or notebook work, run the reported Python with `-m dascore` to stay in the same environment. [Agent onboarding](agents.qmd) covers the `dascore skills` and `dascore skill` commands.

## Targets

Use exact public names such as `Inventory`, `PatchAttrs.tag`, or `dascore.proc.coords.select`, and identifiers such as `tutorial/patch` for authored pages. Select a module page with `module:`, as in `dascore doc module:dascore.viz.waterfall`; when a module re-exports a same-named function, the plain name selects the function. Unknown or ambiguous names print an error and exit nonzero. Output is UTF-8, even when redirected to a file.

## The Markdown corpus

The first request builds a directory of Markdown files from the packaged tutorials, recipes, and API docstrings. Examples are not run. The text works offline; images link to copies hosted on GitHub for the installed release tag or development commit, or the `dev` branch when no commit is recorded. API pages include their defining module and signatures; unbound method signatures include the instance parameter.

The API pages cover core objects, processing, transforms, visualization, built-in namespaces, and selected public utilities, but not external plugins or format-specific APIs. Building them imports the supported modules without creating data objects or running operations; missing optional modules are listed in the summary.

The corpus lives under `docs/<DASCore version>/` in DASCore's user cache, which the `docs_cache_dir` [setting](configuration.qmd) can move, and later commands reuse it. In an editable install, source changes build a new corpus in a new directory even when the version string is unchanged, so run `dascore doc` again for the current path. Each request deletes corpora of the same version unused for a day. To rebuild explicitly:

```bash
python -m dascore doc --rebuild
```

## Search documentation

Point your editor or agent's file search at the directory `python -m dascore doc` reports, which may be outside the project workspace. Titles, API names, body text, and keyword metadata are all searchable. For example, with ripgrep:

```bash
rg -n -i -C 2 -g '*.md' 'filter|bandpass|low.?pass' "/absolute/documentation/path"
rg -l -i -g '*.md' 'inventory|geometry' "/absolute/documentation/path"
```

The first shows matching lines with context; the second lists matching files. Then use `doc` for a known API name or open the Markdown page. If a term finds little, try related scientific vocabulary.

## Author keyword tags

Keep subject keywords with their source. API docstrings list comma-separated terms in a `Keywords` section:

```text
Keywords
--------
filtering, bandpass, low pass
```

The website displays this section, and the local corpus keeps the terms as metadata. Use specific scientific terms and common task vocabulary; keywords describe subjects, not whether a page is an agent skill.
